Lo schwannoma vestibolare è il tumore pi:
Vestibular schwannoma is the most frequent tumor of the cerebellopontine angle. It arises in the internal auditory canal and, as it grows, protrudes into the cistern: the typical "ice cream cone" shape (cone in the canal, scoop in the cistern) distinguishes it from meningioma, which has a broad base on the dura, a dural tail, often calcifications and usually does not widen the canal. Large lesions become heterogeneous, with cysts.
Epidermoid cyst has signal similar to CSF but restricts on diffusion and does not enhance.
The report should state: side, intracanalicular component (up to the fundus of the canal?) and cisternal component, maximum diameter in the cistern, relationships with the pons, peduncle and fourth ventricle (Koos classification: III if it touches the brainstem, IV if it compresses it and displaces the fourth ventricle), hydrocephalus.
Massa dell'angolo pontocerebellare che e: Cerebellopontine angle mass entering the internal auditory canal: vestibular schwannoma until proven otherwise.
Trattato con radiochirurgia Gamma Knife: Treated with Gamma Knife radiosurgery (Vestibular-Schwannoma-SEG collection: patients with a single sporadic vestibular schwannoma, with tumor segmentation).
